relevance_note: A review of vigabatrin therapy in SSADH deficiency whose unnumbered Table summarizes previously published treated patients individually (e.g. '10-year-old boy with autistic features'), plus one earlier patient in the text ('described by Jakobs and colleagues 3 in a boy'); no ALDH5A1 variant is printed for anyone.
method_note: Rows and spans were assembled with a short Python script from my own reading; every span is sliced from the paper's lines and checked verbatim. The paper has a single unnumbered table (cited in the text as '(Table)'); I labelled its rows 'Table 1 row k' because the Author column is a reference column, not a patient label, and copied the Author cell into source_reference_in_review. Row 5 (Gibson et al., 1995, 'Six patients, unblinded') is group-level (a pooled symptom list and 'One patient developed absence- like seizures...' without identifying which patient), so it got no rows; data rows are still counted from the top, so the rows after it are rows 6-8. The table conversion is misaligned: text wraps into the next row ('behavior' / 'problems' across rows 1-2; 'double- blind crossover with' / 'placebo' across rows 1-2; 'slowing on the' / 'EEG' across rows 5-6). Row 1's 'behavior problems' could therefore not be quoted contiguously and was not recorded. Row 2's Posttreatment cell repeats row 1's wording ('Improved ataxia, IQ, speech and motor, no change in behavior and hyperactivity') before 'After initial improvement, vegetative, dystonia, irritability, encephalopathy'; I recorded the cell as printed (including ataxia observed for row 2) but this may be a conversion or typesetting duplication. Features were recorded only where named as present; 'improved/decreased ataxia' in a Posttreatment cell was taken as ataxia present. Improvements in speech, language, concentration or motor skills were not turned into deficits. Ages in the Pretreatment Symptoms column (age at vigabatrin start/report) were recorded as age_at_last_evaluation; no onset or diagnosis ages are given. Row 8 (Matern): pretreatment EEG 'Normal' (EEG abnormality excluded, pretreatment) but EEG slowing during vigabatrin (observed); this is a change over time, not a contradiction, so the checklist item is observed. The text says 'At least two patients developed new onset seizures and worsening of the EEG ... 26'; ref 26 is a single-patient report (Matern row) and the statement could not be tied to specific people beyond that row, so it was not used. The text patient 'In one patient reported by Jaeken and colleagues, 19' is the same as table row 3 (same reference and 70% CSF GHB fall) and was not given a separate row. 'ref 3 patient' (Jakobs and colleagues 3, the first patient) is cited to a different reference from the table's 'Jakobs et al., 1992' (a girl) and was kept separate; not merged with any table row. No ALDH5A1 variant, gene symbol or genetic testing is reported for any individual, so the variants table is empty; diagnosis basis is not reported per person. Hyperactivity was not mapped to 'attention problems or ADHD'.
